title: Lab: Triage a Misbehaving Server
intro_md: A web server is reported down and its disk is filling up. Work through a realistic triage: check disk, find the log hog, inspect the service, free the port, and bring it back.

steps.instruction_md: Check overall disk usage in human-readable form.
steps.mock_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/xvda1       20G   20G     0 100% /
tmpfs           2.0G     0  2.0G   0% /dev/shm
steps.hint: df reports free disk space; add the flag for human-readable sizes.

steps.instruction_md: The root volume is full. Summarize the size of each directory under `/var` (human-readable).
steps.hint: du -s summarizes, -h is human-readable. Glob the children of /var.

steps.instruction_md: `/var/log` holds 18G. List its files sorted by size (largest first) with details.
steps.mock_output:
-rw-r--r-- 1 www-data www-data 17.5G Jul 13 09:12 app.log
-rw-r----- 1 syslog   adm       210M Jul 13 09:12 syslog
steps.hint: ls has a flag that sorts by file size.

steps.instruction_md: Check the status of the failed `api` service with systemd.
steps.mock_output:
● api.service - Example API
   Active: failed (Result: exit-code)
   ...EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::8080

steps.instruction_md: Something is squatting on port 8080. Show listening sockets with process info.
steps.hint: ss with flags for tcp/udp, listening, process, numeric.
SIGTERM (15) asks nicely; SIGKILL (9) is a last resort.
Same systemctl pattern as before, different verb.
